+def pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop):
+    """
+    Lazy max-heap over pair counts (training): heap holds (-count, pair)
+    entries, and for every pair in stats some entry has a count >= its current
+    count (callers push the new count whenever a count increases; decreases
+    are fixed up here when the stale entry surfaces). Returns (top, cands):
+    the maximal count and every pair with that count, i.e. the same as
+    max(stats.values()) and the pairs equal to it. The entries of the
+    candidates are pushed back, so the heap invariant still holds afterwards.
+    """
+    while True:
+        if not heap:
+            raise ValueError("max() arg is an empty sequence")
+        neg, p = heap[0]
+        c = stats_get(p)
+        if c == -neg:
+            break
+        heappop(heap)
+        if c and c < -neg:
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p)) # count went down: re-file it (not 0)
+    top = -neg
+    cands = []
+    while heap and heap[0][0] == neg:
+        p = heappop(heap)[1]
+        c = stats_get(p)
+        if c == top:
+            if p not in cands:
+                cands.append(p)
+        elif c and c < top:
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p))
+    for p in cands:
+        heappush(heap, (neg, p))
+    return top, cands
+
+
+def regex_train(self, text, vocab_size, verbose):
+    # body of RegexTokenizer.train
+    assert vocab_size >= 256
+    num_merges = vocab_size - 256
+
+    # split the text up into text chunks
+    text_chunks = self.compiled_pattern.findall(text)
+
+    # input text preprocessing: identical chunks always merge identically, so
+    # keep each distinct chunk once (in first-seen order) with its multiplicity.
+    # Pair counts and their first-seen order are the same as over all chunks,
+    # so max() picks the same pair, ties included.
+    chunk_counts = {}
+    _count_elements(chunk_counts, text_chunks)
+    ids = [list(ch.encode("utf-8")) for ch in chunk_counts]
+    weights = list(chunk_counts.values())
+
+    # count the number of times every consecutive pair appears (once);
+    # afterwards the counts are updated incrementally for changed chunks only
+    # where[p]: indices of chunks that contain (or once contained) pair p,
+    # possibly repeated; only those chunks can hold an occurrence of p when
+    # it gets merged (chunk visiting order does not matter: chunks merge
+    # independently, and a repeated or stale visit finds nothing to merge)
+    stats = {}
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    where = defaultdict(list)
+    k = 0
+    for chunk_ids, w in zip(ids, weights):
+        for p in zip(chunk_ids, chunk_ids[1:]):
+            stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + w
+            where[p].append(k)
+        k += 1
+    # lazy max-heap of (-count, pair): an entry is valid while it matches
+    # the current count; every pair whose count changes is pushed again
+    heap = [(-c, p) for p, c in stats.items()]
+    heapify(heap)
+
+    # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
+    merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
+    vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # idx -> bytes
+    for i in range(num_merges):
+        # find the pair with the highest count; ties go to the pair whose
+        # first occurrence (chunk order, then position) is earliest, which
+        # is what max() over a freshly recounted dict would pick
+        # (the tie-break does not depend on dict order, so the top pairs
+        # come from the lazy heap; a merged pair's count drops to 0)
+        try:
+            top, tied = pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop)
+        except ValueError:
+            max(()) # no positive count left: max()'s own error
+        pair = tied[0]
+        if len(tied) > 1:
+            # earliest occurrence (chunk, position) among the tied pairs:
+            # where[p] holds every chunk that contains p (plus stale ones),
+            # so visit those in chunk order and stop once past the best
+            best_k = len(ids)
+            best_j = 0
+            for p in tied:
+                for k in sorted(where[p]):
+                    if k > best_k:
+                        break
+                    chunk_ids = ids[k]
+                    for j, q in enumerate(zip(chunk_ids, chunk_ids[1:])):
+                        if q == p:
+                            break
+                    else:
+                        continue # stale entry: p no longer in chunk k
+                    if k < best_k or j < best_j:
+                        best_k = k
+                        best_j = j
+                        pair = p
+                    break
+        # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+        idx = 256 + i
+        # replace all occurrences of pair, updating pair counts
+        regex_merge(ids, weights, where, stats, heap, pair, idx)
+        # save the merge
+        merges[pair] = idx
+        vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]
+        # prints
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")
+
+    # save class variables
+    self.merges = merges # used in encode()
+    self.vocab = vocab   # used in decode()
+

journal.text:
I tried to cut encode_ir in minbpe by moving the body of RegexTokenizer.train out of regex.py into the lazily loaded _train.py, so encoding never pays to load training code. I then tried turning docstrings into comments to trim more.

Evaluation 1 moved train's body and was rejected. encode_ir went from 381222925 to 377723084, ratio 0.9908 against a required 0.9900. Outputs were identical and train_ir was flat at 1.0001. Evaluation 3 added the docstring change and was also rejected, encode_ir ratio 0.9911, train_ir 0.9995. Moving pop_top_pairs too would have given the missing margin, but that change came to 223 lines, over the 200-line limit. I stopped without submitting.

I now think module import cost is a real part of encode_ir here, but trimming regex.py alone sits just short of the threshold. Docstrings are not where the cost is.

Next I want to move pop_top_pairs into _train.py as its own small change, under 200 lines, on top of the train move. Failing that, I should look for actual encode hot-path work instead of import cost.
